title: [Forecast quý 2-2025] Fruit and vegetable consumption
prompt: The world health organization recommends that people should eat five or more portions of fruit and vegetables per day. The bar chart shows the percentage of males and females in the UK who consumed five or more portions of fruit and vegetables per day by age group in 2006.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart illustrates the proportion of men and women in different age brackets in the UK who consumed five or more portions of fruit and vegetables daily in 2006.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, women consistently ate more fruit and vegetables than men across nearly all age groups, except the oldest demographic where rates were equal. Additionally, consumption peaked in the 55-64 age group for both genders, while the 19-24 group had the lowest figures.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding younger demographics, the 19-24 age group recorded the lowest consumption rates at approximately 15% for males and 16% for females. The figures were notably higher for those aged 25-34, reaching around 20% and 22% respectively. Meanwhile, the 35-44 bracket showed males at approximately 22% and females at 25%.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for older age groups, the 45-54 demographic saw roughly 22% of males and 27% of females meeting guidelines. Consumption peaked in the 55-64 group at approximately 33% for men and 35% for women. However, figures declined for those aged 65-74, dropping to about 27% and 29% respectively. Finally, the oldest group aged 75 and above showed equal rates of approximately 25% for both genders.
